newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solana says Russia, NATO could exchange officers.
newsitem.headline: Solana says Russia, NATO could exchange officers.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana has proposed that Russia and the alliance station permanent liasion officers in their respective military commands as part of attempts to build a closer relationship.

Solana said in an article in Monday's edition of the English-language International Herald Tribune newspaper that the proposal was one of many ideas up for discussion to "flesh out the substance of a new, permanent relationship with Russia".

Solana, who on Monday welcomed Russian security supremo Alexander Lebed to NATO's headquarters for talks on the alliance's enlargement plans, said the two sides must build on the cooperation in the current peace mission in Bosnia.
"Why not build on this by having Russian officers permanently at NATO Supreme Command Headquarters and, reciprocally, NATO liaison officers at the Russian General Staff?," Solana wrote.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry proposed at a NATO meeting in Norway late last month that the alliance "throw open its doors" to Russia to help convince its old Cold War foe its intentions were not hostile.

Moscow opposes NATO's plans to take in new members from former communist Europe, but western nations argue the hostility will lessen if the issue runs in tandem with a new deal for Russia giving full weight to its importance in world affairs.

NATO officials said Solana would present a number of proposals to Lebed, including a formal charter covering all aspects of ties between the two, to convince Moscow of it would have a role in an emerging new European security order.

Solana said in his article on Monday: "It is my ardent desire to see a Russia-NATO partnership that fulfills its still untapped potential. For our part, we have set out far-reaching proposals for ever closer political and military relations with Russia."
